title.orig: Stue i Strandgade med solskin på gulvet
title.en: Interior in Strandgade, Sunlight on the Floor
title.zh: 斯特兰德街的起居室，地板上的阳光

institution.name: SMK – Statens Museum for Kunst (National Gallery of Denmark)

image.edit: Trimmed the dark photographic background around the object, then resized.

basis.en: Public domain: the artist died in 1916. SMK marks this image as public domain (Public Domain Mark 1.0).
basis.zh: 公有领域：作者卒于 1916 年。丹麦国家美术馆（SMK）将此图像标为公有领域（公有领域标记 1.0）。

alt.en: A pale grey room with a tall, white-curtained window and a closed white door. A woman in black sits with her back to us at a small table against the wall, and sunlight through the window lays a bright pattern of panes on the bare floor.
alt.zh: 一间浅灰色的房间，有一扇挂着白纱帘的高窗和一扇关着的白门。一位穿黑衣的女子背对我们，坐在靠墙的小桌前；阳光透过窗子，在空荡的地板上铺出明亮的窗格图案。

note.en: The same apartment at Strandgade 30, by day. Hammershøi's wife Ida often posed for him seen from behind, so the room keeps its privacy, and so does she. The real subject is the patch of sun on the floorboards, which will have moved by the time anyone looks up.
note.zh: 同一间斯特兰德街 30 号的公寓，白天。哈默修伊的妻子伊达常背对画面为他做模特，于是房间保有它的隐私，她也一样。真正的主题是地板上那块阳光——等有人抬头时，它已经挪开了。

pick.en: A room, a window, a person at a table, and a square of sunlight that is already moving. The painting asks for nothing and explains nothing, and still holds attention for a long time. I keep it as a reminder that a quiet room with good light is subject enough.
pick.zh: 一个房间、一扇窗、一个伏案的人，和一块已经在移动的阳光。这幅画什么也不要求，什么也不解释，却能长久地留住目光。我留着它，提醒自己：一个光线好的安静房间，本身就足以成为主题。
